Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Global MedTech Solutions Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Reynolds, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Global MedTech Solutions delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance:
1. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
2. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Overall performance highlights and key achievements

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Our organic revenue growth came in at 8.4% year-over-year on a constant currency basis—solidly ahead of our guided range of 6% to 8% and reflecting the strength of our innovation-driven portfolio amid a robust recovery in elective procedures. This marks our sixth straight quarter of accelerating organic growth, underscoring the durability of our franchise in high-growth areas like structural heart and robotics.

To provide full transparency, organic growth excludes the impact of our January acquisition of NeuroStim Dynamics, which added about 1.2 points to reported growth, as well as favorable FX tailwinds of 2.1 points, primarily from a stronger euro and yen. Reported total revenue reached $2.85 billion, up 11.7% as reported.

Let me break this down first by segment, where we saw broad-based strength across our five core franchises: Cardiovascular & Structural Heart, Orthopaedics, Advanced MedSurg, Neuromodulation & Neurovascular, and Vision & Diagnostics.

Cardiovascular & Structural Heart, which is 41% of revenue at $1.17 billion, led the way with 12.6% organic growth, fueled by our market-leading TAVR platform, the VitaFlow Neo, which captured an incremental 180 basis points of share in the U.S. structural heart market, now standing at 28%. Global TAVR procedures grew 14% year-over-year, per our internal tracking aligned with Leerink Partners data, and we outperformed thanks to our next-gen low-profile delivery system, which received FDA approval in March and is ramping to 40% attach rates in U.S. centers. In Electrophysiology, our RhythmSync ablation catheter drove 18% growth, benefiting from expanded indications for AFib treatment following positive OUTPACE trial data presented at Heart Rhythm Society. Margins here expanded 210 basis points to 72%, reflecting procedure mix shift toward high-acuity cases.

Orthopaedics, 22% of revenue at $627 million, posted organic growth of 6.8%, in line with industry volumes as tracked by Definitive Healthcare. Hip and knee reconstruction grew 7.5%, with our Triad Cementless Stem gaining traction in the U.S. ambulatory surgery center channel, where we now have partnerships with over 450 ASCs—up 25% year-over-year. Robotics was a bright spot at plus 22% growth, driven by the rollout of our PrecisionKnee system, which integrates AI-driven planning software akin to Zimmer Biomet's ROSA but with superior soft-tissue balancing algorithms. We faced some pricing headwinds of 50 basis points from GPO negotiations, but offset this via 2% volume gains from enabling technologies.

Advanced MedSurg, 18% of revenue at $513 million, delivered 9.2% organic growth, propelled by our endoscopy portfolio. Single-use endoscopes, like the PureView Duodenoscope, surged 25% amid FDA-mandated duodenoscope reprocessing scrutiny—echoing recalls at Olympus and Pentax—and helped us gain 300 basis points share in GI procedures. Hernia and soft tissue repair grew 11%, leveraging our BioMesh Pro absorbable scaffolds, which saw strong uptake in Europe post-CE Mark expansion.

Neuromodulation & Neurovascular, 12% of revenue at $342 million, accelerated to 10.1% growth, with deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's up 15% on the back of our NeuroPulse MR-compatible leads, compatible with 3T MRI scanners and mirroring Medtronic's Percept platform advancements. Stroke intervention revenues jumped 28% with our Aspire Thrombectomy device, benefiting from guideline updates favoring aspiration techniques over stent retrievers, as seen in the STRATIS registry data.

Vision & Diagnostics, 7% of revenue at $199 million, showed a steady 4.5% organic growth, tempered by softer premium IOL adoption in APAC due to economic headwinds. Our WaveFront-optimized toric lenses grew 8%, however, capturing share from Alcon's Vivity in LASIK-adjacent segments.

Shifting to geography, our U.S. business—67% of revenues at $1.91 billion—grew organically 6.2%, slightly below total as we lap tough COVID comps from the elective procedure rebound. Nonetheless, we outpaced hospital volumes by 250 basis points, per our claims data analysis, driven by 12% growth in outpatient settings where reimbursement parity for ASCs continues to expand under CMS rules.

EMEA, 17% of revenue at $485 million, was our fastest grower at 14.7% organic, with standout performance in Germany and the UK. TAVR volumes surged 20% post-NICE guidelines broadening access, and our endoscopy franchise benefited from French hospital tender wins totaling €45 million. We navigated pricing pressures in Southern Europe via value-based contracts tied to HAI reduction outcomes.

APAC, 11% of revenue at $314 million, delivered 13.9% organic growth, led by China at plus 18% where our TAVR platform achieved NMPA approval in Q1, ramping to 15% market penetration. Japan grew 11% on yen recovery and robotics adoption, while India saw 25% growth from affordable ortho implants amid the Ayushman Bharat expansion.

Emerging Markets rounded out at 5% of revenues with 11.2% growth, highlighted by Brazil's elective procedure normalization and LATAM tender activity.

Strategically, these results validate our 'Innovate to Penetrate' framework: 65% of growth came from new products launched in the last three years, with R&D investment at 9.2% of sales yielding a robust pipeline—10 IDE submissions planned for FY24, including our next-gen robotic platform rivaling Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci in soft-tissue precision. We're also leaning into digital health synergies, with our ProcedureAI analytics suite now live in 2,500 ORs, driving 15% utilization uplift.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 organic growth of 7% to 9%, with full-year trending toward 8%. Risks include supply chain volatility in semiconductors for neuromodulation and potential CMS cuts to ortho bundles, but our 45% gross margins provide ample flexibility.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

We continue to demonstrate disciplined execution amid a dynamic medical devices landscape. As you know, SG&A remains a critical lever for us in an industry facing persistent inflationary pressures on travel, professional fees, and compensation, compounded by regulatory headwinds like EU MDR recertification and U.S. reimbursement scrutiny under CMS's latest IPPS updates. Yet, we've delivered meaningful efficiency gains, enabling us to outperform our peers in expense-to-revenue leverage.

Let me start with the numbers. For the quarter, SG&A expenses came in at $285 million, up just 3% year-over-year, or roughly 150 basis points below our revenue growth of 9.2%. This marks the third consecutive quarter of sequential SG&A deleveraging, with expenses as a percentage of revenue improving 120 basis points to 25.8%—our lowest in over two years. On a trailing twelve-month basis, SG&A efficiency stands at 26.4% of sales, down from 28.1% a year ago and tracking toward our full-year target of 26%. For context, this compares favorably to industry benchmarks: Medtronic reported 27.5% in their last quarter, while Stryker hovered around 28%, per their filings. Our absolute savings year-to-date total $42 million, primarily from productivity initiatives I'll detail shortly.

Breaking it down by category: Selling expenses, which represent 62% of our SG&A bucket, grew only 2% year-over-year to $177 million. This reflects optimized field force deployment amid stabilizing procedure volumes post-COVID—global elective ortho and cardio procedures are now at 98% of 2019 levels, per Definitive Healthcare data. General and administrative costs, at $108 million, were flat sequentially, thanks to aggressive overhead controls.

Regionally, our U.S. operations drove outsized gains, with SG&A as a percentage of local revenue dipping to 24.2%—a 90 basis points improvement—fueled by higher case volumes for our flagship coronary stents and TAVR platforms, like our next-gen EvoFlow valve, which saw 15% procedure growth. We offset 4% wage inflation here through a 5% reduction in non-quota-carrying sales support roles via AI-driven territory mapping tools. In Europe, performance was more challenged, with SG&A up 6% locally due to €25 million in one-time MDR compliance costs for our neuromodulation portfolio, akin to headwinds Boston Scientific flagged last quarter. Excluding those, EMEA efficiency improved 40 basis points to 27.1%, supported by consolidated distributor models in key markets like Germany and France. Asia-Pacific was our star, with SG&A leverage expanding 250 basis points to 22.5% of revenue, driven by lean go-to-market in China—where our structural heart devices captured 12% market share—and India, leveraging digital HCP engagement to minimize field travel amid 20% APAC revenue growth.

Now, turning to the initiatives powering these results. We've embedded a multi-pronged SG&A optimization framework, targeting 200-300 basis points of annual improvement through 2025. Key technical pillars include:

Digital Sales Transformation: Rolled out our Salesforce Einstein AI platform across 85% of our 4,200-person global salesforce, enabling predictive lead scoring and virtual OR simulations. This reduced live demo travel by 18%, saving $22 million year-to-date, while boosting rep productivity—average deals per rep up 12% to 22. Similar to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci remote proctoring, but scaled for our breadth of devices from pacemakers to endoscopy.

Procure-to-Pay Automation: Implemented SAP Ariba across procurement, automating 70% of vendor invoices and yielding $15 million in savings through dynamic discounting and supplier consolidation. We cut indirect spend growth to 1.5% versus 5% industry inflation, per Hackett Group benchmarks.

Zero-Based Budgeting and Headcount Discipline: Conducted our second annual ZBB exercise, scrutinizing every line item. This rationalized G&A headcount by 7% to 1,800 roles, with a revenue-per-headcount ratio now at $1.2 million—up from $1.05 million last year. We shifted 20% of back-office functions to our low-cost Manila shared services center, mirroring Abbott's model.

Data Analytics and KPI Dashboards: Our proprietary MedDev Analytics suite tracks real-time metrics like cost-per-procedure and SG&A burn rate by therapeutic franchise. For instance, in our orthopedics segment—competing with Zimmer Biomet's ROSA robot—we trimmed marketing spend 10% by reallocating to high-ROI KOL engagements.

Strategically, these efforts aren't just cost cuts; they're enablers for reinvestment. We've recaptured $42 million year-to-date to fund R&D in next-gen robotics and digital therapeutics, positioning us against disruptors like Johnson & Johnson's Ottava and Medtronic's Hugo systems. Looking forward, we expect Q3 SG&A at 25.5-26% of revenue, with full-year savings of $65-70 million, assuming flat FX and no further regulatory shocks. Risks include potential U.S. election-driven reimbursement changes or China tariff escalations, but our 65% gross margins provide ample cushion.

In summary, our SG&A discipline underscores the MedTech resilience playbook: leverage scale, digitize ruthlessly, and stay ahead of reimbursement curves. This positions us for 12-15% EPS growth in 2025.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

As we continue to execute on our mission to transform patient outcomes through cutting-edge medical technologies, I'd like to highlight our R&D investment and the robust progress in our innovation pipeline. This remains a cornerstone of our long-term value creation strategy in the $500 billion-plus global medical devices market, where we're targeting high-growth segments like structural heart, neuromodulation, and digital therapeutics.

Let me start with the numbers. In the quarter, we invested $285 million in R&D, representing 13.8% of our quarterly revenue—up 18% year-over-year in absolute dollars and up 120 basis points as a percentage of sales. For the full nine months, our R&D spend totals $812 million, or 13.2% of revenue, putting us on track for a full-year figure around $1.1 billion, or approximately 13% of projected sales. This positions us favorably against peers: our as-reported R&D intensity exceeds Boston Scientific's roughly 11.5% and Abbott's Vascular segment at around 12%, while aligning with Medtronic's approximately 14% in their high-innovation CVG business. We've sustained this elevated spend through disciplined capital allocation—R&D now captures 65% of our OpEx growth—driven by the need to outpace the industry's 8-10% CAGR in structural heart and the accelerating shift toward next-gen therapies amid an aging global population projected to drive 15% demand growth for cardiovascular interventions by 2028, per Grand View Research.

This investment is yielding tangible pipeline momentum across our three pillars: precision interventions, neuro-digital hybrids, and outpatient enablement. We now have 28 programs in our pipeline, with 12 in late-stage development—Phase II/III clinicals or regulatory submission—up from 9 a year ago—and a robust early-stage funnel of 16 preclinical and proof-of-concept initiatives. Our hit rate remains strong at 75% advancement from Phase I to II, bolstered by our proprietary AI-driven lead prioritization platform, which has reduced failure rates by 22% since its 2022 rollout.

Diving into highlights:

Precision Interventions, 45% of R&D allocation at $128 million in the quarter: Our structural heart franchise continues to lead. The crown jewel is our next-gen TAVR platform, EvoFlow Gen2—a fully repositionable, low-profile transcatheter aortic valve replacement system with bioresorbable anchoring and integrated hemodynamic sensors. We completed enrollment in the 850-patient pivotal ORBIT-3 trial ahead of schedule in August, with topline data expected Q1 2025. Early futility analysis shows a 28% reduction in paravalvular leak versus the current market leader, Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra, positioning us for potential 510(k) clearance by mid-2025 and EU MDR approval under our Type IIb pathway. Commercially, this could add $450-600 million in peak U.S. sales by 2028, tapping into the $8 billion TAVR market growing at 18% CAGR.

We've also advanced our drug-eluting bioresorbable scaffold, InnoStent-R, for coronary artery disease. Phase III RESOLVE-2 trial met its primary endpoint of 9-month target lesion failure at 4.2%—non-inferior to Abbott's Xience with a p-value of 0.002—and we've submitted our PMA module to the FDA in the quarter. Regional tailwinds are strong: In the U.S., we're leveraging CMS's expanded TAVR reimbursement for intermediate-risk patients; in Europe, post-MDR recertification, we're seeing 25% sequential uptake; and in China, our NMPA submission for InnoStent-R is under priority review, targeting a market where percutaneous coronary interventions grew 22% year-over-year per IQVIA data.

Neuro-Digital Hybrids, 30% allocation at $86 million: Here, we're pioneering closed-loop neuromodulation for chronic pain and movement disorders, addressing the $15 billion spinal cord stimulator market underserved by incumbents like Nevro and Abbott. Our NeuroLink Adaptive SCS system—featuring real-time AI algorithms that adjust stimulation based on patient biometrics via Bluetooth Low Energy integration—reported 85% responder rates at 12 months in the 400-patient PACE-2 IDE study, surpassing Medtronic's Intellis by 15 percentage points in opioid reduction. We dosed the first patient in our pivotal trial in the quarter and plan FDA IDE approval submission next quarter. Strategically, this hybrid approach aligns with the digital health boom, where FDA has cleared 40+ AI/ML-enabled devices this year alone.

Regionally, Europe's neurostim market is exploding under value-based care pilots in Germany and the UK, where we've secured HTA reimbursement for our legacy SCS; Asia-Pacific represents 20% upside, with Japan PMDA trials initiating Q1 2025 amid a 12% CAGR.

Outpatient Enablement, 25% allocation at $71 million: Capitalizing on the 30% shift to ASCs, our robotics and imaging portfolio is progressing. The InnoArm Flex robotic catheter manipulator hit 95% procedural success in 200-case bench-to-bedside validation, with first-in-human trials starting next quarter under FDA's Q-Sub pathway—mirroring Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci pivot to endovascular apps. In imaging, our AI-powered OCT platform for intravascular plaque characterization achieved CE Mark in July and is in U.S. 510(k) review, promising 40% faster pullbacks and 18% improved stenosis detection accuracy.

Our R&D engine is fueled by $150 million in strategic partnerships this year, including our expanded collab with Siemens Healthineers on hybrid OR imaging and a $75 million J&J milestone payment for co-developing bioresorbable peripherals. We've internalized 60% of manufacturing for scaffolds via our Singapore facility, cutting costs 15% and accelerating time-to-market by 9 months. Risks remain—regulatory scrutiny under FDA's Total Product Lifecycle approach and EU MDR Class III backlogs—but our 4.2-year average development timeline beats the industry 5.1-year norm.

Looking ahead, we expect R&D spend to hold at 13% of sales into 2025, with 4-5 pipeline catalysts: two FDA approvals, three trial readouts, and first sales from our wearable glucose monitor for Type 2 diabetics in partnership with Dexcom-like tech. This pipeline underpins our 12-15% organic growth guidance, with R&D ROI projected at 3-4x over five years based on DCF modeling.

Finally, overall performance highlights and key achievements.

I'm thrilled to discuss our overall performance highlights and key achievements, which underscore another quarter of robust execution amid a dynamic medtech landscape. We delivered record results, driven by our focus on high-growth segments like structural heart, robotics-assisted surgery, and neuromodulation, while navigating macroeconomic headwinds such as persistent inflation in raw materials and supply chain disruptions from Red Sea shipping delays.

Let me start with the top-line numbers. Total revenue reached $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 11% on an organic basis, exceeding our guidance midpoint by 200 basis points. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of double-digit organic growth, outpacing the global medtech market's estimated 6.2% CAGR through 2028, per recent Grand View Research data. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.72, a 25% increase from $1.38 last year, with operating margins expanding 210 basis points to 28.4%—our highest in five years—thanks to disciplined cost management, including a 15% reduction in SG&A as a percentage of sales through digital sales force optimization and AI-driven inventory forecasting.

Breaking it down by segment, our Cardiovascular franchise, which now represents 42% of revenue, surged 18% organically to $1.2 billion. Key driver here was the continued ramp of our EvoHeart TAVR platform, which captured 22% U.S. market share in structural heart, closing the gap on frontrunners like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3. We implanted over 12,000 units globally in the quarter, up 35% year-over-year, bolstered by positive real-world evidence from our ULTIMATE registry showing a 28% reduction in 1-year all-cause mortality versus competitor benchmarks. Neuromodulation grew 16% to $650 million, fueled by the FDA approval and early U.S. launch of our PrecisionAI SCS system—the industry's first AI-adaptive spinal cord stimulator that dynamically adjusts waveforms based on patient biometrics, reducing recharge frequency by 40% and driving a 150 basis points mix shift to premium rechargeable implants.

In Robotics and Endoscopy, up 22% to $520 million or 18% of total revenue, our da Vinci-inspired Orion Surgical System hit a milestone with 1,500 systems installed worldwide, generating $180 million in recurring instrument and service revenue—a 30% year-over-year jump. Utilization rates climbed to 285 procedures per system annually, surpassing Intuitive Surgical's fleet average, thanks to our proprietary haptic feedback tech that improves precision in soft-tissue procedures by 22%, per independent OR cadaver studies. Orthopedics and Spine rounded out at $480 million, flat organically but with underlying strength in our Mako-like Triad robotic arm, which saw 25% procedure growth in joint reconstruction amid a rebounding elective backlog.

Regionally, U.S. revenue of $1.7 billion grew 16%, supported by favorable CMS reimbursement for our TAVR and SCS portfolios under the 2024 IPPS final rule, which preserved pass-through status for five SKUs. EMEA delivered 12% organic growth to $650 million despite PMA-equivalent scrutiny from the MDR, where we secured CE Mark renewals for 18 devices ahead of schedule. APAC was the star at 20% growth to $400 million, led by China where our joint venture with a local distributor expanded EvoHeart access, capturing 15% share in a market projected to hit $10 billion by 2027. Emerging markets like LATAM and India contributed $100 million, up 25%, via low-cost neuromodulation kits tailored for tier-2 hospitals.

Key achievements this quarter include three strategic milestones. First, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of NeuroVive Therapeutics, adding their gammaTile brain tumor implant to our neuro portfolio and immediately accretive by $0.05 to EPS. This bolsters our $3.5 billion addressable market in neuro-oncology, where brachytherapy adoption is rising 12% annually. Second, R&D investment hit $420 million or 14.7% of revenue—above our 13-14% target—yielding 14 FDA 510(k) clearances, including our EchoAI intravascular ultrasound platform that integrates real-time AI lesion characterization, reducing procedural time by 18% in our pivotal trial versus Philips' Volcano benchmark. Third, sustainability progress: we achieved 25% reduction in Scope 3 emissions through reshoring 40% of nitinol supply to U.S. facilities, mitigating tariff risks and aligning with EU Green Deal mandates.

Strategically, these results affirm our 'Innovate, Expand, Optimize' framework. We're gaining share in a $550 billion global medtech market by prioritizing procedure-enabling technologies—robotics TAM alone is $25 billion growing at 15% CAGR. Our 36-month pipeline includes the Genesis CRM leadless pacemaker, entering IDE trials next quarter, and a next-gen wearable glucose monitor rivaling Dexcom's G7 for hospital-to-home transitions. Looking ahead, we reiterate FY24 organic growth guidance of 11-13% and margins of 27-28%, with conviction from a $14 billion backlog and 92% customer retention.

In summary, this quarter exemplifies Global MedTech Solutions' resilience and leadership, positioning us to deliver sustained value for patients, providers, and shareholders.

I will now turn the call over to Michael for a review of our financial results.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter.

Starting with the P&L, total revenue of $2.85 billion exceeded expectations, with gross margins expanding to 45%, up 120 basis points year-over-year, driven by favorable product mix in high-margin structural heart and robotics, as well as manufacturing efficiencies from our Singapore facility. Operating expenses were well-controlled, with R&D at 13% of sales and SG&A deleveraging to 25.8%, resulting in operating income of $810 million and adjusted operating margins of 28.4%.

Adjusted EPS of $1.72 grew 25%, reflecting the margin expansion and share repurchases of $200 million under our ongoing program. GAAP EPS was $1.45, impacted by acquisition-related charges.

On the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and equivalents, up from $3.8 billion last year, supported by operating cash flow of $650 million. Debt stands at 2.2x EBITDA, within our target range, providing flexibility for pipeline investments and bolt-on M&A.

For guidance, we now expect full-year organic revenue growth of 8-10%, adjusted EPS of $6.75-$6.90, and operating margins of 27.5-28.5%. Q3 organic growth of 7-9%, as Elena noted. This assumes stable FX and no major disruptions.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Elena for Q&A.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, on the organic growth, can you expand on the TAVR share gains in the U.S. and how the VitaFlow Neo is performing relative to Edwards' Sapien?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, John. The VitaFlow Neo has been a standout, capturing those extra 180 basis points to reach 28% share, thanks to the low-profile delivery system now at 40% attach rates. We're outperforming on procedure growth at 14% globally, with real-world data showing better paravalvular leak reduction, aligning with our ORBIT-3 trial progress. This positions us well against Sapien 3 Ultra as we ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Michael, on SG&A, those efficiency gains are impressive—can you talk about the sustainability into next year, especially with MDR costs and potential inflation?

Michael Reynolds:
Absolutely, Lisa. The multi-pronged framework—digital sales via Einstein AI, procure-to-pay with Ariba, ZBB, and analytics—is embedded for 200-300 bps annual improvement through 2025. YTD savings of $42 million fund R&D, and even excluding one-time MDR hits in EMEA, we're at 26.4% TTM. With gross margins at 65% cushion, we see Q4 at 25.5-26%, supporting 12-15% EPS growth in 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Hi, team. Raj, on the R&D pipeline, what's the update on NeuroLink Adaptive SCS and any regulatory risks with the AI components?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, David. NeuroLink is progressing strongly—85% responder rates in PACE-2, beating Intellis on opioid reduction, with first pivotal patient dosed. The AI/ML is under FDA's Total Product Lifecycle, and we've seen 40+ clearances this year. IDE submission Q4, with Europe HTA support. Risks are managed via our 75% hit rate and 4.2-year timelines.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
Thanks. Elena, just on guidance—how do supply chain risks factor into the raised FY outlook, especially semiconductors for neuromodulation?

Elena Vasquez:
Emily, supply chain volatility is a noted risk, but our 45% gross margins and reshoring efforts—like 40% nitinol to U.S.—give flexibility. The $14 billion backlog and 92% retention underpin 11-13% organic growth. Emerging markets and APAC ramps, like China TAVR at 15% share, offset any semi hiccups.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of Global MedTech Solutions. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
